title.value: SARS-CoV-2 infection in Africa: a systematic review and meta-analysis of standardised seroprevalence studies, from January 2020 to December 2021
title.justification: The title directly captures the main focus and scope of the study, which is a systematic review and meta-analysis of SARS-CoV-2 seroprevalence in Africa.
title.quote: SARS-CoV-2 infection in Africa: a systematic review and meta-analysis of standardised seroprevalence studies, from January 2020 to December 2021

extractions.description: The paper is a systematic review and meta-analysis estimating the seroprevalence of SARS-CoV-2 in Africa using population-based studies during the COVID-19 pandemic. It assesses the extent of exposure to the virus, identifies demographic and geographical variations in seroprevalence, and discusses implications for public health measures and vaccination strategies.

climate_change_is_central.justification: The paper primarily focuses on COVID-19 seroprevalence and does not directly address themes related to climate change.
climate_change_is_central.quote: Estimating COVID-19 cumulative incidence in Africa remains problematic due to challenges in contact tracing, routine surveillance systems and laboratory testing capacities and strategies.

primary_category.justification: As the paper is focused on COVID-19 seroprevalence in Africa and does not address climate change, it does not fit into any predefined climate change categories.
primary_category.quote: Estimating COVID-19 cumulative incidence in Africa remains problematic due to challenges in contact tracing, routine surveillance systems and laboratory testing capacities and strategies.

primary_sub_category.justification: The paper does not engage with specific climate change sub-categories, focusing instead on public health aspects of COVID-19.
primary_sub_category.quote: We aimed to better understand SARS-CoV-2 epidemiology in Africa up to and before the emergence of the Omicron variant.
